scenes.say: On June thirtieth, nothing happens at Redwood River Supply. No sale, no payment. And yet the accountant still has entries to make. Why?

sub: Made at the end of a period so revenues
and expenses land in the right period
scenes.say: Adjusting entries are made at the end of an accounting period so that revenues and expenses are recorded in the period they belong to, not just when cash changed hands.

scenes.heading: Three ideas behind them
items: Periodicity: cut time into months, quarters, years
Expense recognition: match to the revenue
scenes.say: Three ideas sit behind them. The periodicity assumption chops the life of a business into months, quarters and years. The revenue recognition principle records revenue when it's earned. And the expense recognition principle matches each expense to the revenue it helped earn.

scenes.heading: Four types of adjustment
scenes.say: There are four types. Two are deferrals, where cash moved first: prepaid expenses and unearned revenues. Two are accruals, where cash hasn't moved yet: accrued revenues and accrued expenses. Depreciation, a kind of prepaid expense, is the fifth one you'll see.
Here's a rule to remember. An adjusting entry never involves cash. It always changes one balance sheet account and one income statement account.

scenes.q: Which account will an adjusting entry never include?
scenes.say: Quick check. Which account will an adjusting entry never include? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's C, cash. Cash transactions were already recorded when the money moved.

scenes.say: Pay for something in advance and you haven't spent it yet. You've bought an asset. The adjustment comes when you use it up.

sub: Paid in advance, recorded as an asset,
then expensed as it is used up
scenes.say: A prepaid expense is a cost paid in advance, like insurance, rent or supplies. It starts life as an asset and becomes an expense as it's used.

scenes.heading: June 1 · Buy a year of insurance
scenes.say: On June first, Redwood River pays twenty-four hundred dollars for twelve months of insurance. Debit prepaid insurance, an asset. Credit cash.

scenes.heading: June 30 · Adjust for one month
scenes.say: By June thirtieth, one month of cover has been used: twenty-four hundred divided by twelve is two hundred. Debit insurance expense two hundred, credit prepaid insurance two hundred. Twenty-two hundred stays on the balance sheet.

scenes.heading: Supplies work the same way
scenes.note: Bought 600 of supplies; a count shows 150 left, so 450 were used.
scenes.say: Supplies work the same way. Redwood River bought six hundred dollars of supplies. A count on June thirtieth finds one hundred and fifty left, so four hundred and fifty were used. Debit supplies expense, credit supplies.

scenes.q: Rent of $3,000 is paid for 3 months on June 1. The June 30 adjustment?
opts: Dr Rent expense 1,000, Cr Prepaid rent 1,000
scenes.say: Quick check. Three thousand dollars of rent is paid on June first for three months. What's the June thirtieth adjustment? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's B. One month is used, so debit rent expense one thousand and credit prepaid rent one thousand.

scenes.say: A customer pays you before you've done the work. Great for cash. But you haven't earned it yet. So what is it?

sub: Cash received before the work is done
A liability until it is earned
scenes.say: It's unearned revenue: cash received in advance for goods or services not yet delivered. Until you deliver, you owe the customer, so it's a liability.

scenes.heading: June 10 · Customer prepays
scenes.note: Prairie View Dairy pays for six months of equipment servicing.
scenes.say: On June tenth, Prairie View Dairy pays three thousand dollars up front for six months of equipment servicing. Debit cash, credit unearned revenue, a liability.

scenes.heading: June 30 · Earned one month
scenes.say: By June thirtieth, one month's servicing is done: three thousand over six months is five hundred. Debit unearned revenue five hundred, reducing the liability. Credit service revenue five hundred.

sub: Earned as the work is done,
scenes.say: So the liability shrinks and revenue grows as the work gets done. Gift cards, subscriptions and season tickets all work this way.

scenes.q: On the June 10 entry, what kind of account is unearned revenue?
scenes.say: Quick check. When the dairy prepaid on June tenth, what kind of account was unearned revenue? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's C, a liability. Despite the name, it isn't revenue until it's earned.

scenes.say: Sometimes the work is done or the cost is incurred, but no one has billed anyone yet. Those are accruals.

sub: Earned but not yet billed or received
scenes.say: Accrued revenue is revenue earned but not yet billed or collected. You record a receivable and the revenue.

scenes.heading: June 30 · Unbilled repair work
scenes.note: Work finished June 29; invoice goes out in July.
scenes.say: Redwood River finished seven hundred dollars of repair work on June twenty-ninth but won't send the invoice until July. Debit accounts receivable, credit service revenue.
An accrued expense is a cost incurred but not yet paid. Wages and interest are the classic examples.

scenes.heading: June 30 · Wages owed
scenes.note: Staff worked June 27–30; payday is July 3.
scenes.say: Staff worked June twenty-seventh to thirtieth but won't be paid until July third. That's six hundred dollars of wages. Debit wages expense, credit wages payable.

scenes.heading: June 30 · Interest on the note
scenes.say: And interest builds up on the five thousand dollar note at six percent a year. One month is five thousand times six percent times one twelfth, twenty-five dollars. Debit interest expense, credit interest payable.

scenes.q: Employees earned $1,200 not yet paid. Which entry?
opts: Dr Wages expense, Cr Wages payable
scenes.say: Quick check. Employees have earned twelve hundred dollars that hasn't been paid yet. Which adjusting entry? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's B. Debit wages expense, credit wages payable. No cash has moved yet.

scenes.say: Redwood River's equipment will last years. So charging its whole cost as an expense in June would be wrong. Depreciation fixes that.

sub: Spreading the cost of a long-term asset
over the periods that use it
scenes.say: Depreciation spreads the cost of a long-term asset, like equipment or a truck, over the periods that benefit from using it. It's not about market value. It's about matching cost to use.
Redwood River's equipment cost eight thousand dollars and should last five years with no salvage value. That's sixteen hundred a year, or about one hundred thirty-three dollars a month.

scenes.heading: June 30 · Monthly depreciation
scenes.say: The adjusting entry debits depreciation expense one hundred thirty-three and credits accumulated depreciation.

scenes.heading: On the balance sheet
scenes.say: Accumulated depreciation is a contra asset. It sits under equipment and reduces it, without touching the original cost. Eight thousand less one thirty-three gives a book value of seven thousand eight hundred sixty-seven.

scenes.q: What kind of account is accumulated depreciation?
scenes.say: Quick check. What kind of account is accumulated depreciation? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's C, a contra asset. It has a credit balance and reduces the asset it belongs to.

scenes.say: Once the adjustments are posted, you run the trial balance again. This one is the version your financial statements are built from.

scenes.heading: From unadjusted to adjusted
scenes.say: Start with the unadjusted trial balance. Make the adjusting entries. Post them to the ledger. Then prepare the adjusted trial balance.

scenes.heading: What changed at Redwood River
scenes.say: At Redwood River, the adjustments added twelve hundred dollars of revenue, from the dairy contract and the unbilled repair, and fourteen hundred and eight of expenses, from insurance, supplies, wages, interest and depreciation. Prepaid accounts shrank and new payables appeared.

sub: Each adjustment had equal debits and credits
scenes.say: Because every adjusting entry had equal debits and credits, the adjusted trial balance must still balance. If it doesn't, an adjustment was posted wrongly.
Now every balance is up to date, and the financial statements can be prepared straight from it. That's the next lecture.

scenes.q: Why is the adjusted trial balance prepared?
opts: To check balances after adjustments, before statements
scenes.say: Quick check. Why do we prepare an adjusted trial balance? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's B. It checks that the ledger still balances after adjustments, and it's the source for the statements.
